slot_note: seed ET19 used for its decision and quantity (an ESG data company's published emissions intensity built across EPA's greenhouse gas reporting, production statistics and keys that join many-to-many); its own world (CAMD and GHGRP joined to EIA plant data through the EPA-EIA crosswalk) is task459's pack, so the intensity is a gas producer's methane intensity measured from aerial surveys
niche: measurement-based methane intensity of gas producers from repeated aerial plume surveys, for an emissions data company's low-methane rating
answer: Rate four Tollaver Basin producers low-methane for 2027: Calbrent Energy, Ostrel Energy, Corrandale Petroleum and Brushy Mesa Operating (0.104, 0.108, 0.119 and 0.134 per cent against the 0.20 line; Ashmund Production, the nearest of the rest, at 0.232).
stakeholder_role: the head of methane ratings at an emissions data company that rates a basin's gas producers for the buyers of their gas

spine.entity: one well's reported gas production for one month, original or amended
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a state oil and gas commission's well production reports)

world.geography: an unnamed US state's gas basin (invented), twelve producers

driver: The decisive quantity is a period total of many intermittent sources seen only through a few snapshot surveys, each of which records a source only while it is active and then only with a probability that rises with its size, so a blank at a surveyed place is partly a miss: each detection has to stand for the instances its detection probability implies, measured on blind trials of known size, while counting blanks as zeros understates the units whose total sits in many small sources and carrying each detected source through the period overstates the units whose total sits in large intermittent ones.
driver_concrete: Each producer's methane over the rating year to 30 September 2026 is the time-averaged emission rate of its sites over four basin-wide aerial campaigns, each plume weighted by one over the survey's probability of detecting a plume of its rate (measured on the provider's blind controlled releases), not the campaigns' detected plumes alone with blanks as zeros (which understates producers whose methane leaks from many 5 to 15 kg/h sources) nor each detected source at its detected rate all year (which overstates producers whose methane comes from tank dumps part of the time).
stump: The default path averages each producer's plume rates over its passes and campaigns, counting every imaged site without a plume as zero, and rates eight producers low-methane, among them Anchell, Pinyon Draw, Pellisto and Ashmund (0.150, 0.155, 0.179 and 0.181 per cent), whose methane leaks from many 5 to 15 kg/h sources a pass catches less than half the time; carrying each detected source through the year instead rates none; only weighting each plume by one over the detection probability at its rate, fitted to the provider's blind controlled releases, rates the golden four.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who attributes every plume to its producer, reads every field and applies the rating standard averages each producer's detected rates over its passes and campaigns with a blank counted as zero and rates eight producers low-methane, four of them over the 0.20 per cent line though it puts them at 0.150, 0.155, 0.179 and 0.181 per cent.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a producer's measurement-based methane intensity, built the way methane inventories build it from aerial surveys (plume rates weighted by a detection probability that depends on rate and wind, measured on controlled releases, averaged over campaigns against the methane in the gas produced); with another field's nouns the rate- and wind-dependent detection of intermittent plumes and the produced gas's methane content no longer read.

differentiation.task180: task180 forecasts a plant's earthquake count once a network change removes the daily masking of its small events (completeness varying with the hour); task462 estimates a time-averaged emission total from four snapshot surveys whose detection probability rises with each plume's rate, each detection standing for the instances its probability implies: no forecast of a record change and no time-of-day masking
differentiation.task255: task255 fits a severity distribution's tail with each claim truncated at its deductible and censored at the retention; task462 fits no size distribution: it weights each detected plume by the survey's detection probability at its rate, measured on blind releases, and averages the campaigns to a total
differentiation.task456: task456 classifies unit-days from three imperfect categorical records with a latent class model; task462 scales one instrument's continuous detections by its measured detection curve across repeated snapshots of intermittent sources

layer1: several sources for one picture: the survey provider's plume detections and flight-line coverage, the state commission's well production reports, the producers' site register, gas composition analyses and the producers' greenhouse gas reports
imperfect keys: plumes located by coordinates and attributed to the nearest site, a few between two producers' pads; wells and sites that changed operator during 2026; one site under two spellings
vintages and revisions: amended production reports superseding the originals; one campaign's rates reprocessed by the provider
units and time: plume rates in kg per hour, production in Mcf, reports in metric tons, survey passes stamped in UTC
genuine overlap: plumes imaged twice on overlapping flight lines in one campaign
real coverage: flight lines lost to cloud, a few sites not imaged in a campaign
